text:
noah_prod: Proposal: per-tenant quantization profiles (customers can opt into aggressive quant for cost savings). We need a safe rollout plan that balances quality regressions vs cost. Putting a strawman here for feedback.

tara_ml: +1. Important: every quant profile must have an eval suite (prompt set) and an expected quality delta bound. If not, block rollout.

leo_sre: Ops constraints: quant changes can affect memory and latency. Rollout must include small canaries, capacity headroom, and automatic fallback if p95 latency or error rate increases.

anya_devex: Console UX: three-state per-tenant control: off (baseline), canary (select tenants), profile (named quant profile). Expose a preview modal showing expected token savings and sample outputs.

jaz_cs: Customer note: some customers want to test on staging first; we should offer a "trial bucket" they can opt into with a revert button. Also need a one-click rollback.

auditbot: action: created policy draft for feature_flag: routing.quant_profiles.v1 (owner: product/noah_prod).

noah_prod: Rollout stages (draft):
1) Internal QA + baseline evals (no tenants)
2) Manual pilot: 2 trusted tenants, manual opt-in, 48h, human review of sample outputs
3) Tenant-slice canary: 1% tenants, automatic gating on telemetry (72h)
4) A/B experiment: matched cohort control vs quant profile for 7 days to measure quality/regression and cost
5) Ramp to 25% over 5 days if metrics stable, then GA opt-in

tara_ml: Metric gating: primary = quality regression measured by evaluation prompts (delta pass rate), secondary = p95 latency delta, error rate (5xx), token_cost_pct. Define per-tenant baselines and use relative thresholds.

leo_sre: Router-enforced fallback rules:
- On eval_fail_rate > configured threshold for tenant -> immediately revert tenant to baseline profile
- On sustained pool p95 > baseline + 25ms for 2m -> divert tenant to fallback pool
- On 5xx increase > 1% absolute -> pause rollout and page oncall

anya_devex: Feature flag example (flat JSON for Admin API):
```
{name: "routing.quant_profiles.v1", profiles: ["baseline","quant-8bit","quant-4bit-aggr"], pilot_tenants: ["redwood-internal"], auto_sample_pct: 1, gates: {quality_drop_pct: 2, p95_ms: 25}, kill_switch: true}
```

noah_prod: Experiment plan: pair similar-tenants by traffic shape and run matched A/B; require 95% confidence that average quality_drop < 2% OR cost savings > 8% to consider positive. Also manually review failure cases for false positives.

jaz_cs: Comms: will prepare pilot invite email + FAQ explaining tradeoffs and revert steps. Legal wants a short clause that beta features may change model outputs.

leo_sre: Ops checklist before tenant-slice canary:
- Dashboards: per-tenant quality_pass_rate, p50/p95/p99, token_cost, fallback_count
- Alerts: quality_drop > gate -> P0; pool_p95 > baseline + 20ms -> P0
- Reserve 12% spare capacity in quant pools for rollback
- Runbook: how to force revert profile for tenant(s) via Admin API

anya_devex: Admin API examples for quick revert:
```
PATCH /admin/tenant/{id}/flags
body: {"routing.quant_profiles.v1": "baseline"}
```
Response: 200 + audit_id

noah_prod: Privacy and auditing: do not log prompt texts with quant_variant metadata. Keep routing-level debug logs 7d and aggregated metrics 180d. Audit events for flag flips must include user id and reason.

tara_ml: Also add a small offline regression harness that replays sampled requests through quant profiles nightly for drift detection. If nightly drift exceeds thresholds, auto-open an investigation ticket.

leo_sre: Emergency kill switch requirement: global button in Console to set all tenants to baseline profile and create an incident channel. Must emit audit and page SRE.

jaz_cs: Timeline request: can we start staging next week and tenant-slice canary in 2 weeks? I can recruit pilot customers.

noah_prod: Sounds reasonable. Action items: tara to own eval suites + offline harness; leo to own runbook + alerts; anya to wire Console toggles + API; jaz to recruit pilots; i'll draft RFC and rollout playbook. Target: staging by next Wed.

auditbot: note: policy draft linked in #policies.
